fixes.explanation: Tamar's a real name in the Bible, baker, but she's not in this story. She's the Tamar who shows up in Genesis 38:6. Joshua says, “Only Rahab the prostitute and all those with her in her house will live, because she hid the spies we sent.” (Joshua 6:17) Rahab is the one who hid the spies, and that's the reason the text gives. Her house is the one that gets spared.

Deborah shows up later in the Bible as a judge (Judges 4:4), but she has no part in Jericho. Listen to who Joshua names: Rahab, the woman who hid the spies. Her whole household was spared, “…all those with her in her house…” (Joshua 6:17) That's a lot of people covered by one brave choice.

problems.problem: The claim that Tamar is a name in the Bible comes from outside the passage and needs a reference.
The claim that Deborah was a judge comes from outside the passage and needs a reference.
